column3: “Let fall, and in you” is rendered “even of yourself, let go”; the Hebrew is difficult.
“Bush” is a rare word (perhaps a juniper); “see” and “parched places” are rendered “see … prosperity” and “stony wastes.”
NASB follows the reading tradition “fear” (the written text “see”).
“My disloyal ones” follows the written text; NASB reads “Those who turn away.”
“From a shepherd” is rendered “from being a shepherd,” and “a day incurable” as “the woeful day.”
“The gate of the sons of the people” is rendered “the public gate.”
